03 / EVIDENCE & METHODS

Know what sits behind a number.

Geometry, model predictions, numerical checks and physical measurements have distinct roles.

Download provenance
A / THE MODEL

Power-law-based
retention models.

The ligament is the material left between an opening and the tooth-root region. Opening area and ligament thickness define a geometry penalty. The reciprocal transformation converts this penalty into retained safety factor.

R̂ = 1 / (1 + P)

Exponential load mixing is used by primary static model E. Harmonic load combination is used by secondary static model H. Power-law terms in opening area and ligament thickness predict static and fatigue safety-factor retention relative to a solid gear. The fatigue model retains exponential load mixing.

Why “power-law-based”?

The geometry penalty includes φnbR−m. The full retention expression also contains the reciprocal transformation and a load-combination rule, so it is more precise to call it a power-law-based retention model than a pure power law.

Ten layouts.
Every outcome retained.

C / THE NUMERICAL CONTEXT

Inspect the fields.
Keep their scope in view.

These are 40-tooth, scale-0.800 screening-mesh illustrations under the T reference at tooth position 31. They are separate from the 42- and 46-tooth layouts on the Explore page. Stress is unsmoothed; the outlines are undeformed.

The wider programme retains 2,452 accepted fields. Local refinement of four matched 42-tooth geometries changed final-step retention by up to 2.60% statically and 2.12% in fatigue. Absolute safety factors remain mesh-dependent.

What has been checked physically?

The earlier aluminium prototype provides a separate strain comparison. The present reference-steel numerical programme is not a completed experimental validation of every atlas entry. Matched steel strain measurements, production-route fatigue tests and measured process inputs remain further assessment work.
